title: [Free Plugin ] CT_NotetagGuardian -  Notetag Validator & Warning Helper ( RPG Maker MZ Plugin )

posts.author: CynthiaTools
posts.body:
Hi everyone, I'm sharing a small free utility plugin for RPG Maker MZ.
This is a free RPG Maker MZ utility plugin designed to help catch suspicious or malformed notetag formatting during playtest.
If you work with a lot of plugins, a lot of note boxes, or large messy databases, this plugin can help you spot bad lines before they turn into long debugging sessions.
What it does​
scans your project notes during playtest
reports suspicious formatting in the console
shows a quick in-game summary popup
supports ignored tags
includes a full warning report scene
supports deep map and event note scanning
Why I made this​
Once a project gets bigger, notetags become very easy to mess up.
A missing >
A broken copied line
A weird leftover tag from an old plugin
A malformed custom note from 2am brain damage
…and suddenly something stops working and you have to waste time hunting it down.
CT_NotetagGuardian was made to help reduce that nonsense.
Best for​
plugin-heavy projects
large RPG Maker MZ databases
developers cleaning up old note data
users who rely heavily on custom note systems
You can download it free now on the link below.

Changelog - CT_NotetagGuardian v1.0.2 - Whitelist / Ignore Patch
Changed from v1.0.1:
- Added whitelist/ignore support for custom notetag syntax.
- Added Ignore Comparison Operators parameter. Default: true.
- Treats <=, >=, and => as operator text instead of broken bracket syntax.
- Added Allow Double Angle Tags parameter. Default: false.
- When enabled, whole-line syntax like <<Tag>> or <<Tag: value>> is accepted.
- Added Allow Backslash Closing Tags parameter. Default: true.
- Whole-line syntax like <Tag\> is accepted.
- Added Ignored Line Contains parameter.
- Lets users skip warnings for lines containing exact snippets such as <=, =>, <<, or custom plugin text.
- Added Ignored Line Regexes parameter.
- Advanced JavaScript regex whitelist for custom syntax.
- Kept existing Ignored Tags behavior, but routed it through the new whitelist layer.
- Shortened popup summary text slightly and increased popup window height from 132 to 144 to reduce cutoff risk.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Special thanks to ShadowDragon for testing NotetagGuardian in MV and pointing out useful custom syntax edge cases.
Because of that feedback, this update now adds whitelist options for custom notetag syntax and ignores `<=` / `>=` / `=>` operators by default to reduce false positives.
You can check out ShadowDragon’s itch page here:
ShadowDragon - itch.io

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
It's an interesting idea. Just to offer a suggestion, based on your screenshots, having multiple lines describing the same (suspected) error in different ways could be more confusing than helpful to some users.
Or perhaps at least hide half of them behind a "verbose" plugin parameter.
The typical way one would read such things is that if I see multiple errors reported for a line, I would expect that to mean there are multiple errors on that line, not the same error described multiple ways.
Thanks for sharing your work.

CT_NotetagGuardian v1.0.3 - Compact Warning Output Patch
Applied against:
- Latest uploaded file: [10]CT_NotetagGuardian.js
What changed:
1. Added plugin parameter:
- Detailed Warning Mode
- Default: false
2. Default output is now compact:
- When multiple checks describe the same suspicious note line, the plugin reports one clearer warning for that line.
- Example root issue: incomplete/unbalanced tag.
- This reduces the chance users think one bad line has many separate errors.
3. Detailed output is still available:
- Set Detailed Warning Mode = true to restore the old style where every diagnostic reason is printed separately.
Validation:
- JavaScript syntax check passed with node --check.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Special Thanks to ATT_Turan — for his valuable suggestion.
I’ve updated **CT_NotetagGuardian v1.0.3 - Compact Warning Output Patch** based on ATT_Turan suggestion.
The plugin now has a new **Detailed Warning Mode** parameter. By default, warning output is more compact, so if multiple checks are pointing at the same suspicious notetag line, it shows one clearer warning instead of making it look like that line has many different errors.
For users who still want the older full diagnostic style, they can turn **Detailed Warning Mode = true**.
You can check out and support ATT_Turan, in development game here:
